description: Original TOEFL-style Take an Interview questions for vocabulary transfer. Difficulty tags are editorial estimates, not empirically calibrated.

questions.prompt: Thanks for participating. First, when you're learning something new, do you usually prefer to study independently or with guidance from a teacher? Why?
questions.example_html: Digital resources <mark>enable</mark> me to study at my own pace.

questions.prompt: I see. Can you describe a resource or experience that has helped you learn something on your own?
questions.example_html: Giving students more choice can <mark>empower</mark> them to manage their learning.

questions.prompt: Some students struggle to take responsibility for their learning. What could teachers do to help these students become more confident and independent?
questions.example_html: Regular feedback can <mark>encourage</mark> students to practise consistently.

questions.prompt: Last question. Do you think students should have more control over what and how they learn, or is it better for schools to make most of those decisions? Why?
questions.example_html: Independent projects can <mark>empower</mark> students to take responsibility for their progress.

questions.prompt: To begin, what kinds of activities do you enjoy outside your regular classes or work?
questions.example_html: Volunteer work can <mark>enrich</mark> students' understanding of their communities.

questions.prompt: Interesting. Have you ever taken part in an activity that helped you learn something you wouldn't normally learn in a classroom? Tell me about it.
questions.example_html: Practical workshops <mark>enhance</mark> skills that lectures alone may not develop.

questions.prompt: Imagine that a university wants to improve its students' educational experience. Would you recommend investing in cultural activities, practical workshops or new technology? Why?
questions.example_html: The university could <mark>enlarge</mark> its library collection to support research.

questions.prompt: Finally, some people believe that universities should focus mainly on academic knowledge, while others think they should also help students broaden their perspectives. Which view do you agree with?
questions.example_html: Exposure to other disciplines can <mark>enrich</mark> students' perspectives.

questions.prompt: Thank you for joining us. What rules or policies have you encountered at school or university that you found particularly useful?
questions.example_html: Schools should <mark>enforce</mark> rules consistently and fairly.

questions.prompt: Some rules are followed more consistently than others. Why do you think students sometimes ignore rules even when they understand them?
questions.example_html: Clear explanations can make it easier to <mark>enforce</mark> reasonable policies.

questions.prompt: Suppose your university was considering a new policy to reduce noise in study areas. What kind of policy would you recommend, and how should the university make sure students follow it?
questions.example_html: The university could <mark>enact</mark> a formal regulation on quiet study areas.

questions.prompt: One final question. Do you think students should have a formal role in deciding university policies that directly affect them? Why or why not?
questions.example_html: Students should be <mark>entitled</mark> to express their views on policies that affect them.

questions.prompt: First, what digital tools do you usually use to organize your notes, assignments or other information?
questions.example_html: I <mark>embed</mark> reminders in my digital calendar to stay organized.

questions.prompt: Thanks. When you need to remember complicated information, do you prefer written notes, diagrams or digital tools? What makes your preferred method useful?
questions.example_html: Simple diagrams can <mark>encapsulate</mark> the main idea of a lecture.

questions.prompt: Imagine that a university is designing an online learning platform. What features should be built into it to help students understand and remember important information?
questions.example_html: Designers could <mark>embed</mark> practice quizzes directly into the platform.

questions.prompt: Last question. As more personal and academic information is stored digitally, do you think universities should prioritize making that information easy to access or keeping it secure? Explain your view.
questions.example_html: Institutions can <mark>encode</mark> information in standardized formats, although sensitive data also requires secure protection.

questions.prompt: Thanks for taking part. What qualities do you think make a school or university a welcoming place for students?
questions.example_html: A welcoming campus should <mark>embody</mark> respect and inclusion.

questions.prompt: Can you think of a person, group or organization that represents values you admire? What do they do that demonstrates those values?
questions.example_html: Her actions <mark>embody</mark> the values she promotes.

questions.prompt: Suppose a university wants to improve student well-being. Which areas of student life should its support programs address?
questions.example_html: Student-support programs should <mark>encompass</mark> academic and social needs.

questions.prompt: Finally, do you think universities are responsible for making sure all students have equal opportunities to succeed, or should that primarily be an individual responsibility? Why?
questions.example_html: Universities should <mark>ensure</mark> that support services are accessible to everyone.

questions.prompt: To start, when you spend time on a school or university campus, do you prefer indoor or outdoor spaces? What do you like about them?
questions.example_html: Green spaces offer a place to relax without <mark>endangering</mark> wildlife.

questions.prompt: I see. Have you ever noticed a change to a public or school space that affected how people used it? What happened?
questions.example_html: The city decided to <mark>enclose</mark> the garden to protect newly planted trees.

questions.prompt: Imagine that a university plans to build a new facility in an area currently used as a garden. What concerns should university officials consider before making a decision?
questions.example_html: Construction could <mark>endanger</mark> local biodiversity unless the project is carefully planned.

questions.prompt: Last question. Why do you think schools and other institutions sometimes find it difficult to change long-established practices, even when those practices create problems?
questions.example_html: Long-established procedures can <mark>entrench</mark> inefficient practices.
